title.narrative: Every child needs a good teacher (Mali)

description.narrative: Mali has made progress in improving access to education over the last few years but education statistics are still bleak. According to the World Bank in 2010, one in four children (half a million in total) do not go to primary school at all and only just over half complete primary school. A major reason for this is that there are not enough trained teachers, particularly outside the public education system. About 40% of children attend community or religious schools as opposed to government schools, mainly in rural areas. These schools have played a pivotal role in increasing access to education, but the vast majority of teachers are not qualified and many are not trained. There is a government policy in place to progressively transform community schools into public schools in Mali over the next five years. Many community teachers hope this will offer a pathway towards qualification and formalisation of their status. This application aims to improve the quality of teaching in Mali by incorporating a locally-developed ‘competence framework' into teacher training to ensure that all teachers reach a nationally accepted standard for qualification. This will be used to help integrate a large number of community teachers into the formal education system. The approach will be piloted in Ségou, one of eight provinces in Mali. All 2,500 community teachers in Ségou will be part of a professional development programme to upgrade their skills. At the same time, the partners will advocate for community teachers to achieve the same status as public teachers in the long-term and popularise the content of the competence profile in different regions, so that parents, teachers and children also know what to expect of a ‘good' teacher. Pupils, as well as teachers, will benefit. Over 80,000 children go to community schools in Ségou. The project expects to achieve a 20% increase in the number of these pupils passing annual exams and completing primary school on time.
